A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConsFormer research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison; v2 retains Appendices A–D and adds E–I.

before.justification: v1 reports original ConsFormer experiments on Sudoku, graph coloring, and nurse scheduling, including performance comparisons and ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original MAXCUT, multi-start, output-function, baseline, and direct-gradient-descent experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix F implements optional multi-start inference: several candidates are updated concurrently, and a solution is accepted when any candidate becomes feasible. v1 discussed pool-based extensions only as future work. The core Transformer architecture, single-step training, and constraint penalties remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds MAXCUT, extending evaluation from constraint feasibility to cut optimization. Training uses random 100-vertex graphs, while evaluation uses GSET graphs with 800–10000 vertices, including weighted graphs. The original Sudoku, coloring, and nurse-scheduling coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds evaluated Greedy Coloring, OR-Tools Feasibility Jump, and OR-Tools Random Search comparisons to the retained coloring baselines. The new MAXCUT comparison also includes SDP, RUNCSP, ECO-DQN, and ECORD, with reference scores drawn from prior work as identified in Section 4.3.

E3.justification: Original experimental settings are retained, but v2 adds substantially different evaluation designs: MAXCUT gap metrics and 180-second runs, Gumbel-Softmax versus softmax at temperatures 0.1 and 1, candidate-pool sweeps under a 10-second budget, and OR-Tools tests at 30 and 60 seconds. Appendix I adds 10000-step direct SGD tests measuring satisfied Sudoku constraints.

E4.justification: New analyses distinguish output sharpness from Gumbel noise (Appendix E), test multi-start pool size and iteration tradeoffs (F), examine sensitivity to comparator runtime (G), and test direct variable optimization as Sudoku difficulty increases (I). The original subset-selection and positional-encoding ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports averages across 10 runs for direct SGD in Appendix I and specifies 20 parallel MAXCUT runs in Appendix G. These disclosures concern added experiments; they do not establish additional repetitions of the retained results. Neither version supplies confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original Tables 2–3 and positional-encoding results are unchanged. New results include MAXCUT percentage gaps of 0.31, 0.34, 0.43, and 1.27 across size groups. New multi-start variants reach 55.67% and 15.00% on the two coloring OOD sets, compared with retained single-start results of 47.33% and 11.92%. Tables 9, 11, and 12 add further ablation and baseline outcomes.

T1.justification: Appendix H adds a formal discrete ALLDIFFERENT violation-degree function and connects it to the existing penalty-design rationale. The original CSP formulations, continuous penalty equations, and zero-penalty feasibility condition are retained. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain self-supervised single-step learning, the importance of positional information, iterative OOD generalization, and leading neural performance on OOD Sudoku. The abstract names the expanded benchmark evidence, but the contribution statements and conclusion retain their scientific meaning.

C2.justification: New Section 5 explicitly states that parametric constraints, such as SAT clauses with variable negations, cannot be handled without richer constraint inputs. New discussions interpret Gumbel noise as aiding large-instance search, explain direct SGD failures through local optima and lack of transfer, and acknowledge ANYCSP's superior MAXCUT performance.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a GitHub implementation link and adds MAXCUT settings to Appendix D: four layers, three heads, embedding size 128, and selection probability 1.0. It also identifies implementations used for the added coloring baselines. Previously documented hardware, optimizer, training budget, and original model configurations remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly connects ConsFormer to constraint-based local search and adds references concerning learned SAT search, self-supervised constrained optimization, probabilistic relaxations, and set-function extensions. These broaden the existing positioning without replacing its organizing argument. Publication updates to already cited works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. Changes include clarifying multi-head attention, separating limitations and future work from the conclusion, adding explanatory appendices, and inserting acknowledgments and an impact statement. The main narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with the MAXCUT table and Tables 9–12, including an expanded coloring comparison. It adds a MAXCUT hyperparameter column and redraws Figure 2 to show output distributions and selected updates more explicitly. Existing plots and tables are also reformatted or relocated; their renumbering alone is not counted.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1 by testing output-function choices, direct optimization, competing heuristics, and runtime sensitivity, while examining scalability on much larger MAXCUT instances. The explicit limitation concerning parametric constraints materially improves the account of applicability, and the implementation link improves reproducibility information. These additions strengthen evidence and transparency, including unfavorable comparisons, although uncertainty reporting remains limited.
